concerns.text: The primary analysis uses a Repeated‑Measures ANOVA on false‑memory *rates* (proportions of “Yes” responses to lure items). Because each rate is derived from only 20 binary trials per condition, the normality and homoscedasticity assumptions of ANOVA are likely violated. In psychology, proportion data with limited trial counts are typically modeled with a binomial GLMM (or transformed with an arcsine‑square‑root) as the primary analysis. Relying on ANOVA as the main test risks inflated Type I error and undermines the validity of the claimed effect (SC‑001, SC‑002). The plan should either (a) make the GLMM the primary analysis and treat ANOVA as a descriptive supplement, or (b) apply an appropriate transformation and verify ANOVA assumptions before proceeding.
